The apostrophe in "isn't" is U+0027, as in the source (B1 MCPProbe.swift:21, B2 :22 and B3 :21 all have byte 0x27). The OD-PENDING-19 resolution note in porting/owner_decisions_pending.md quotes the sentence with U+2019 and says U+2019 is "kept", on the pending question's premise that the source uses U+2019, which the source contradicts; the recommendation the owner accepted (decision_batch_20260922.md B5) replaces only the command. ENGINEERING DECISION: keep U+0027; the conflict is escalated so the owner record can be corrected.

records.title: MCPCatalogEntry.fill substitutes every {key} with the user's value or the field's default
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/MCP.swift:132-147 fill(_:values:) - :135 var value = values[field.key].flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 } ?? field.defaultValue ?? "" | :136 let token = "{\(field.key)}" | :138 value = value.trimmed | :144 out = out.replacingOccurrences(of: token, with: value)

The replacement value is values[field.key] when present and non-empty, else field.defaultValue, else the empty string. Every occurrence of the token in the text is replaced by Foundation's replacingOccurrences(of:with:) with no options (not .literal), so matching is by Unicode canonical equivalence, as is the Swift String dictionary lookup values[field.key]; for ASCII keys and text this is the same as an exact ordinal match. Fields not referenced in the text have no effect. Tokens naming keys that are not fields of the entry are left untouched.

source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Models/MCP.swift:137-143 the "://" + token branch of fill - :137 if out.contains("://" + token) { | :138 value = value.trimmed | :139 for scheme in ["https://", "http://"] where value.lowercased().hasPrefix(scheme) { | :140 value = String(value.dropFirst(scheme.count)) | :142 while value.hasSuffix("/") { value.removeLast() }

records.title: value(for:of:) is a strict draft-then-store-then-default chain
records.action: The key panel or the custom editor renders a field.
records.expected_result: If drafts[entry.id]?[field.key] exists (even as the empty string) it wins outright and is returned. Otherwise, if field.kind is .secret, read the credential store for (entry.id, field.key) and return it when non-nil; if the kind is NOT .secret, read connections[entry.id]?.values[field.key] and return it when non-nil. These two are an if/else-if on kind, not a fallthrough: a .secret field never reads the connection's plaintext values, and a .text or .path field never reads the credential store. Failing all of that, return field.defaultValue, and failing that, the empty string.

records.expected_result: Any existing probe task for that id is cancelled first. The connection is the existing one or a new MCPConnection(catalogID: entry.id), and its isEnabled is forced to true - connecting a server that the user had switched off switches it back on.
side_effects: cancels an in-flight probe task, which for a stdio probe terminates its child process through the probe's defer
records.persistence: the connection row is written by the save later in the same call
failure_cases: none
records.cancellation: this IS the cancellation path for a previous probe
records.windows_path: Same. The cancel must actually stop a running stdio probe and kill its child.
records.verification_method: unit plus an interaction test pressing Connect twice quickly

records.title: Pointing an OAuth server at a different address signs it out first
records.preconditions: An OAuth entry with a draft that changes a field used in its URL (in the shipped catalog only gitlab's instance).
records.action: The user edits the instance and presses Sign in.
records.expected_result: When entry.isOAuth and a draft exists, compare entry.oauthURL(values: connection.values) with entry.oauthURL(values: connection.values merged with the draft, draft winning). If they differ, call MCPOAuth.signOut(serverID:) - which deletes the credential-store items "MCP <id> oauth" and "MCP <id> oauth-client" - and MCPProxy.shared.unregister(serverID:). The browser flow then runs afresh against the new address.
side_effects: removes the proxy route for that id
records.persistence: the OAuth session and registered client for that server are destroyed
failure_cases: none; a sign-out of a server that was never signed in is a no-op
records.windows_path: Same comparison of filled URLs, same two deletions from Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3).
records.verification_method: unit driving the two oauthURL values, plus an integration test that the token store is empty afterwards

records.title: disconnect cancels the probe, destroys the entry's secrets, signs an OAuth server out, and forgets the connection, its values and its draft
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:114-128 disconnect(_:) - /// Forgets the connection, its values and its secrets, and removes it from every provider config. probes[entry.id]?.cancel(); probes[entry.id] = nil; MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server: entry); if entry.isOAuth { MCPOAuth.signOut(serverID: entry.id); MCPProxy.shared.unregister(serverID: entry.id) }; connections[entry.id] = nil; states[entry.id] = nil; drafts[entry.id] = nil; save(); exportAll()
records.action: The user picks Disconnect from a connected row's or custom row's menu.
records.expected_result: In this order, with no early exit: cancel and clear the probe task for that id; MCPKeychain.deleteAll(server: entry), whose own contract is PR-MCP-228; if entry.isOAuth, MCPOAuth.signOut(serverID:) and MCPProxy.shared.unregister(serverID:), in that order and only for an OAuth server; connections[id] = nil; states[id] = nil; drafts[id] = nil; save(); exportAll(). The server disappears from the Connected section and from every provider config file. Nothing here is conditional on the server being connected: a failed server takes the same path.
side_effects: deletes one protected-storage item per declared field, plus two more for an OAuth server
rewrites or deletes claude.json, codex.json, copilot.json and gemini-settings.json
calls MCPHub.reload, stopping any in-app client processes for that server
records.persistence: the connection row leaves mcp.json; secrets leave protected storage
failure_cases: a field the entry no longer declares keeps an orphaned protected-storage item
a store that refuses a deletion: upstream reports success anyway; nth reports the failure (OD-0008 A12, PR-MCP-228)
records.windows_path: Same order. A stored secret that fails to delete is reported to the user instead of a silent success, and the rest of the sequence still runs, an ENGINEERING DECISION recorded in the deviation (OD-0008 A12, PR-MCP-228). Disconnect is reached from the connected row menu, the custom row menu and a confirmed custom-server Delete (PR-MCP-073). Secrets live in Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3).
records.verification_method: integration test asserting the call order and the four config files afterwards; with the store refusing a deletion, the failure is reported to the user and the rest of disconnect still runs, while a missing item is not reported

records.title: MCPKeychain.deleteAll destroys one stored secret per field the ENTRY declares, under the account "MCP <id> <field key>", and a deletion that fails is reported
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift:25-31 - /// Forgets every secret the entry declares. The entry, not its id: a custom server /// is not in the catalog, so looking it up there would silently delete nothing. static func deleteAll(server entry: MCPCatalogEntry) { for field in entry.fields { delete(server: entry.id, field: field.key) } }

DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift:21-23 delete(server:field:) - APIKeychain.delete(account(server:field:)); DroppyCode/Services/Providers/APIKeychain.swift:76-83 - a kSecClassGenericPassword query with kSecAttrService = service (default AppInfo.name) and kSecAttrAccount = the account, passed to SecItemDelete with the result DISCARDED
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPKeychain.swift:6-8 - private static func account(server: String, field: String) -> String { "MCP " + server + " " + field }
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:118 - the one call site inside disconnect
records.preconditions: A catalog entry or custom-server entry with zero or more declared fields.
records.expected_result: One delete per field the ENTRY object declares, iterated in the entry's own field order. The account string is the literal "MCP ", the server id, a single space, and the field's key - three parts joined by single spaces, with no separator characters of any other kind. The service is AppInfo.name, one service for the whole app. Upstream discards the delete result, so a missing item, a locked store and a refusal are indistinguishable and none is reported. nth checks it (OD-0008 A12): a failed deletion is reported to the user instead of a silent success. Two details are ENGINEERING DECISIONS, not ruling text (see the deviation): an item that did not exist is not a failure, and the rest of disconnect still runs (PR-MCP-061). The report reads exactly "Disconnected, but Credential Manager did not remove this server’s stored values." (OD-0012 E6); where it is shown is not given by the source or by the ruling (open_question). Crucially the fields come from the ENTRY, not from a catalog lookup by id: a custom server is not in the catalog, so looking it up there would iterate an empty field list and silently delete nothing. An entry with no declared fields deletes nothing and is not an error. A field the entry NO LONGER declares keeps an orphaned item forever, because nothing enumerates the store.
side_effects: One stored secret destroyed per declared field, unrecoverably
a failed deletion is reported to the user
records.persistence: The secrets leave Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3) permanently; they must be re-obtained from the provider.
failure_cases: A locked or unavailable store: upstream deletes nothing and disconnect still reports success; nth reports the failed deletion
An entry whose declared fields changed since the values were written leaves orphans
records.windows_path: Use Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3) and destroy exactly the items the entry declares under the same three-part account string. Check each deletion and report a failure other than "not found" (OD-0008 A12). Reached from disconnect (PR-MCP-061) and from a confirmed custom-server Delete (PR-MCP-073, OD-0008 A1). Never fall back to a plaintext store if protected storage is unavailable.
records.verification_method: integration test asserting one delete per declared field with the exact account string, a no-op for an entry with no fields, that a custom server's fields are taken from the entry rather than the catalog, and that a store refusing a deletion produces a reported failure instead of success

records.title: setEnabled flips the switch, saves and re-exports, and does nothing without a connection
records.action: The user toggles the switch on a connected row or a connected custom row.
records.expected_result: If there is no connection row for that id, the call returns doing nothing at all (no save, no export). Otherwise isEnabled is set, the connection is stored, save() writes mcp.json, and exportAll() rewrites the provider configs, the proxy route table and reloads the hub. Switching a server off removes it from all four provider config files; switching the last one off deletes those files.

replaces the proxy route table and reloads the hub
failure_cases: none
records.windows_path: Same guard and same side-effect set.

records.title: A successful probe writes the tools and version only when a connection row still exists, but always marks the state connected
records.preconditions: A probe returns a result and the task is not cancelled.
records.expected_result: try Task.checkCancellation() first. Then, only if connections[entry.id] exists: set connectedAt = now, serverVersion = result.serverVersion, tools = result.tools and store the row. Unconditionally: states[entry.id] = .connected(toolCount: result.tools.count); save(); exportAll(). When the row was removed in between (a refresh after a disconnect), the card shows Connected with a tool count while enabledServers excludes it, nothing is persisted and no provider gets it. This divergence is upstream behavior and is reproduced.
side_effects: rewrites the four provider configs, the proxy routes and reloads the hub
the page plays the settle chime and runs the celebration animation (PR-MCP-203)
records.persistence: connectedAt (ISO-8601), serverVersion and tools in mcp.json, only when the row exists
failure_cases: the row-missing case leaves a connected badge with no backing record
records.cancellation: a cancelled task returns before any of this
records.windows_path: Reproduce the guard exactly: do not hoist the three writes out of the if, and do not move the states write into it.
records.verification_method: unit reproducing the disconnect-then-refresh race

records.title: An OAuth probe that is refused once signs out, unregisters and probes a second time
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:316-327 the two catch clauses inside startProbe
records.preconditions: The resolved server has a non-nil oauthUpstream.
records.action: The first probe throws MCPProbeError.unauthorizedOAuth, or MCPProbeError.http with status 401 or 403.
records.expected_result: Both catch clauses do the same three things: try Task.checkCancellation(); MCPOAuth.signOut(serverID:); MCPProxy.shared.unregister(serverID:); then call probeOnce again. probeOnce, finding the server no longer signed in, runs the full browser sign-in, re-registers the proxy route and probes through it. There is exactly one retry: a second failure propagates to the outer catch. Both clauses are guarded on resolved.oauthUpstream != nil, so a plain HTTP server that answers 401 is not retried.

removes then re-adds the proxy route
opens the user's browser for a fresh sign-in

a cancellation between the two attempts aborts silently

records.windows_path: Same two clauses, same single retry, same cancellation check placement. Protected storage is Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3), under the same account strings.
records.verification_method: contract fixture: a stub MCP server answering 401 once then succeeding

records.title: probeOnce signs in, registers the proxy route, then probes through the route
records.action: The probe task runs one attempt.
records.expected_result: If resolved.oauthUpstream is non-nil: when MCPOAuth.isSignedIn(serverID:) is false, run MCPOAuth.signIn(serverID:serverName:url:) with the entry's name and the upstream address, which opens the browser and waits; then always call MCPProxy.shared.register(serverID:upstream:headers: [:], usesOAuth: true). Finally call MCPProbe.probe(resolved) - which, because resolve pointed url at the proxy, goes through the local route exactly as every provider will. For a non-OAuth server the whole block is skipped and the probe runs directly.

records.title: Any other probe error becomes a failed state carrying the error's own message

records.title: saveCustom trims the name, mints the id once, and validates against every taken id
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPStore.swift:150-160 saveCustom(_:replacing:) - :151 let old = oldID.flatMap { id in customs.first { $0.id == id } } | :154 if let old { taken.remove(old.id) } | :156 server.name = server.name.trimmed | :159 server.id = old?.id ?? MCPCustomServer.makeID(server.name) | :160 if let error = MCPCustomError.validate(server, existingIDs: taken) { return error }
records.preconditions: The custom editor's Add server or Save is pressed.
records.expected_result: The old server is looked up by oldID among customs. taken = every catalog id plus every custom id, minus the old server's own id when editing. The name is trimmed of whitespace and newlines. The id is old?.id when editing and MCPCustomServer.makeID(trimmed name) when adding - a rename NEVER changes the id, so the connection row and the stored secrets stay where they are. MCPCustomError.validate is then run against taken; on failure the error is returned and NOTHING is written: no customs change, no file write, no probe cancellation.
failure_cases: empty name -> "The server needs a name."

records.title: MCPCustomServer.makeID slugs the name and always yields a usable custom- id
records.preconditions: A new custom server is being added.
records.action: The id is minted from the first name.
records.expected_result: Lowercase the name. Walk its characters: a letter or a number is appended; any other character appends a single "-" but only when the previous appended character was not already a dash (lastWasDash starts true, so leading separators produce nothing). A trailing "-" is removed. The result is "custom-" + the slug, or "custom-server" when the slug came out empty. Examples: "My Server" -> "custom-my-server"; "!!!" -> "custom-server"; "  a  b  " -> "custom-a-b".
records.persistence: the id is persisted in custom-mcp.json and used as the protected-storage account prefix and the provider-config key
failure_cases: a name that slugs to an id already taken is rejected by validate with the takenName message
records.windows_path: Same algorithm character by character. Unicode letters and digits count as letters and numbers, so a non-ASCII name produces a non-ASCII id, which then becomes a JSON key and part of a proxy route path. records.title: The stdio probe waits for each reply on its stdio connection, with the time left before its deadline as that request's timeout
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPProbe.swift:97-114 nextReply - :98 let remaining = deadline.timeIntervalSinceNow | :99 guard remaining > 0 else { | :100 throw exitError(code: nil, isOAuth: isOAuth, stderr: connection.errorTail) | :103 let reply = try await connection.request(method, params, timeout: remaining) | :104 try checkReply(reply) | :109 throw exitError(code: code, isOAuth: isOAuth, stderr: connection.errorTail) | :111 throw exitError(code: nil, isOAuth: isOAuth, stderr: connection.errorTail)
records.action: The probe waits for the matching reply.
records.expected_result: Before each request (initialize, then each tools/list page) the time left before the probe's deadline is computed; when it is zero or less, exitError(code: nil, ...) is thrown without sending anything. Otherwise the request is sent through MCPStdioConnection.request with that remaining time as its timeout (PR-MCP-235), and the reply carrying the request's id is awaited (PR-MCP-232, PR-MCP-233). When the reply arrives, checkReply runs and the reply is returned. When the connection reports the child's exit (PR-MCP-234), exitError(code: <the exit status>, ...) is thrown. When the timer wins, exitError(code: nil, ...) is thrown. exitError always receives connection.errorTail, the last 4000 bytes of stderr (PR-MCP-236). There is no polling interval: the wait ends as soon as the reply, the exit report or the timer arrives. Replies for ids the probe is not waiting on are kept by the connection, not discarded.
failure_cases: exit -> "The server quit (exit <code>). <last non-empty stderr line>" or "The server quit (exit <code>)."
deadline passed before or during a request -> "The server didn't answer in time."
either of the above becomes "Sign-in was rejected. Sign in again in your browser." for an mcp-remote server whose stderr tail contains Unauthorized or invalid_grant (PR-MCP-110)
records.cancellation: a cancelled probe task abandons its pending request and CancellationError propagates out of the wait (PR-MCP-235); the deferred connection.stop() then ends the child
records.windows_path: Event-driven: end the wait the moment the matching reply, the exit report or the timer arrives, with no polling interval. Use the time left before the deadline as each request's timeout, and keep replies for other ids.
records.verification_method: unit with a scripted server: a reply for another id before the awaited one, an exit mid-request, and a deadline reached between pages
records.b3_note: 1.7.0 replaced the 5 ms polling loop, which discarded replies for other ids, with MCPStdioConnection's continuation wait raced against the remaining deadline, which keeps them.

records.title: A stdio failure is classified as unauthorized OAuth, an exit code, or a timeout
records.preconditions: The child exited or the deadline passed.
records.expected_result: When isOAuth is true AND the stderr text passed in contains either the substring "Unauthorized" or "invalid_grant" (case-sensitive), return .unauthorizedOAuth. Otherwise, when an exit code is present return .exited(code:stderr:), and when it is nil return .timedOut. The stderr text is the connection's errorTail: only the LAST 4000 bytes the child wrote to stderr, decoded as UTF-8 (PR-MCP-236), so a marker written before those bytes is not seen. The exited message uses the LAST non-empty trimmed line of that tail.
failure_cases: see the three messages in PR-MCP-120
records.windows_path: Same two substring checks and the same precedence, applied to the same 4000-byte tail. This branch is unreachable for the built-in catalog (see PR-MCP-106).
records.verification_method: unit over the three outcomes, plus an Unauthorized marker written more than 4000 bytes before the end of stderr, which must not be seen
records.b3_note: 1.7.0 passes only the last 4000 bytes of stderr (errorTail) where B2 passed the whole buffer of up to 64000 bytes.

records.title: A probed or hub stdio child is stopped by closing its stdin, a terminate signal, and a kill of the pid alone 3 seconds later
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:120-129 terminate - :122 writeQueue.async { try? handle.close() } | :123 guard process.isRunning else { return } | :124 process.terminate() | :126 DispatchQueue.global().asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + 3) { | :127 if process.isRunning { kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL) }
records.action: The probe finishes, fails or is cancelled, or a hub client stops.
records.expected_result: The stdin write handle is closed on the process's serial write queue, whether or not the child is still running. If the child is not running, nothing else happens. Otherwise the terminate signal (SIGTERM) is sent to the child, and 3 seconds later, on a background queue and not awaited, the child is killed with SIGKILL if it is still running. Both signals go to the child's pid alone, never to its process group, so a grandchild such as the node process npx starts is signalled by neither. The probe and every hub client stop their children this same way.
side_effects: terminates and possibly kills the child process
failure_cases: a child that ignores the terminate signal is killed 3 seconds later
a grandchild the child started is not signalled and can outlive it
records.cancellation: this IS part of the cancellation cleanup
records.windows_path: Stop through the port's StdioProcess termination ladder (ED-126): close stdin, then the graceful stop to the child, then TerminateProcess on that pid alone at +3 s with no job object. The B2 windows_path asked for a whole-tree kill after one second because npx starts node as a grandchild; upstream B3 signals the pid alone after 3 seconds. UNRESOLVED (B3_PLAN.md 6.1 O3): whether the port keeps a tree kill for MCP children needs an owner ruling.
records.verification_method: integration test with a stand-in server that ignores the graceful stop, asserting that its stdin reaches EOF first and that the kill lands 3 seconds later
records.open_question: B3_PLAN.md 6.1 O3: ED-126 (3 s, pid only, as upstream B3) or a whole-tree kill (a job object or a pid-tree kill) for MCP hub and probe children, which npx leaves with a node grandchild.
records.b3_note: 1.7.0 removed the hub's and the probe's own terminate (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL to the process group after 1 s when the child led one) in favour of StdioProcess.terminate: stdin closed, SIGTERM, then SIGKILL to the pid alone after 3 s.

records.title: Stdio stdout is framed on 0x0A with trailing CR and spaces stripped and a final unterminated line delivered at EOF, and stderr is capped at 64000 bytes, keeping the last 16000
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioFramer.swift:19-34 append in the .lines framing - :27 guard let newline = buffer[search...].firstIndex(of: 0x0A) else { | :31 messages.append(Data(buffer[start..<newline])); and :63-69 finish, which hands back the unterminated remainder

DroppyCode/Core/Support/StdioProcess.swift:147-157 deliver and finishOutput - :149 while let last = line.last, last == 0x0D || last == 0x20 { line.removeLast() } | :150 guard !line.isEmpty, let message = JSONValue.parse(line) else { return } | :155 if let remainder = state.withLock({ $0.framer.finish() }) { deliver(remainder) }
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPWire.swift:139-150 launch, which uses the default .lines framing for the probe and the hub alike
records.preconditions: A probe or a hub client is reading from its stdio child.
records.action: Bytes arrive on stdout or stderr.
records.expected_result: stdout bytes accumulate; every 0x0A byte ends one line, and a partial line is held until it completes. Each line loses any trailing 0x0D and 0x20 bytes; an empty line or one that is not valid JSON is dropped, and every other parsed value is delivered as a message. When stdout closes, or 1 second after the child exits, a final line with no terminating 0x0A is delivered the same way instead of being lost. stderr accumulates and, whenever it exceeds 64000 bytes, is replaced by its last 16000 bytes; failure reports read only its last 4000 bytes (PR-MCP-236). A hub child's stderr is buffered the same way and never read. Every step is serialized under the process's lock.
failure_cases: a server that writes a very long line with no newline is parsed only when stdout closes, so a request waiting on it times out first
records.cancellation: stopping the connection closes stdin and ends the child (PR-MCP-111); the message stream finishes when stdout closes
records.windows_path: Same framing on 0x0A only, with trailing CR and space bytes stripped (so a CRLF server works) and the final remainder delivered at EOF. Same two byte caps.
records.verification_method: unit feeding split writes, a CRLF line, an unterminated last line at EOF and an oversized stderr
records.b2_change: Moved and restructured: B1 :383-425 (NSLock and vars, `@unchecked Sendable`) -> B2 :381-430, B2 :384 private final class StdioConversation: Sendable { | B2 :392 private let state = Mutex(State()). The hand-rolled lock around plain var fields became a Swift Mutex (Synchronization) holding a State struct, with the same critical sections; no behaviour change. The 64_000 cap, the 16_000 suffix, the 0x0A split and the draining takeLines are the same.
records.b3_note: 1.7.0 deleted the probe's StdioConversation (and the hub's HubConversation) in favour of StdioProcess and StdioFramer, which strip trailing CR and spaces, deliver an unterminated last line at EOF, and keep a hub child's stderr instead of discarding it.

records.preconditions: A 2xx response whose Content-Type contains text/event-stream.
records.expected_result: When the POST carried no JSON-RPC id (the notifications/initialized notification), the body is nil at once and the stream is never read. Otherwise the stream is read line by line as it arrives. For each line, trim whitespace; skip it unless it starts with "data:"; take the remainder after those five characters and trim it; parse it as JSON; accept it only when it is an object whose "id", read as an integer (an integer, a finite double truncated toward zero, or a string Int() parses), EQUALS the request's id. The first such value is returned immediately, without waiting for the stream to end, so a server that holds the stream open does not hang the caller. A frame for another id, a notification frame without an id and anything unparseable are skipped. When the stream ends without a match the body is nil.

records.windows_path: Read the event stream incrementally and return at the first matching frame; do not buffer the whole body. Every later line with a colon contributes a header: the name is the text before the first colon, trimmed and lowercased; the value is the text after it, trimmed. An empty name is skipped. records.title: The proxy refuses chunked request bodies and bodies over 32 MiB, and truncates a short body silently
records.expected_result: A transfer-encoding header whose value lowercased contains "chunked" answers 411 with {"error":"chunked request bodies are not supported"}. contentLength = max(0, the integer parse of content-length, or 0 when absent or unparseable) - a negative value therefore becomes 0. records.title: An upstream 401 on an OAuth route is retried once with a re-fetched token, which is usually the same token
records.preconditions: An OAuth route relayed a request.
records.expected_result: Ask MCPOAuth.accessToken for the server again with try?; on success set the Authorization header to the new bearer value and re-send the identical request once, then use that response. There is no second retry. Because accessToken only refreshes when a stored expires_at is within 90 seconds, a session stored without expires_in has no expiry and the second call returns the very same token, making the replay a byte-identical retry that gets the same 401. There is no forced-refresh path anywhere. This is upstream behavior and is reproduced.
records.persistence: a successful refresh rewrites the stored session
failure_cases: a missing HTTP response after the replay throws and becomes 502 {"error":"upstream request failed"}
records.windows_path: Reproduce including the useless replay. Add no force-refresh parameter and synthesize no expires_at when the provider omits expires_in.
records.verification_method: contract fixture with a stub answering 401 twice and asserting exactly two upstream requests

records.title: The proxy copies back only Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id and Cache-Control, dropping WWW-Authenticate
records.expected_result: In this order, and only when present upstream: Content-Type, Mcp-Session-Id, Cache-Control. Every other upstream header is dropped, including WWW-Authenticate. A 401 from an OAuth upstream therefore reaches the client bare, and RFC 9728 protected-resource discovery cannot work through a proxy route. This is upstream behavior and is reproduced.
failure_cases: a client attempting discovery through the route sees a 401 with no challenge
records.windows_path: Copy back exactly those three plus the framing headers. Adding WWW-Authenticate would change what providers see.
records.verification_method: contract fixture asserting the response header set

records.title: An event-stream response is relayed as chunked transfer with one chunk per line
source_evidence:
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPProxy.swift:374-394 the SSE branch of writeBack - :379 var buffer = Data() | :381 buffer.append(byte) | :382 if byte == UInt8(ascii: "
") { | :383 await send(connection, Self.chunk(buffer)) | :387 if !buffer.isEmpty { | :388 await send(connection, Self.chunk(buffer)) | :392 await send(connection, Data("0

".utf8))
DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPProxy.swift:413-418 chunk - :414 var frame = Data((String(payload.count, radix: 16) + "\r\n").utf8) | :415 frame.append(payload) | :416 frame.append(Data("\r\n".utf8))
records.expected_result:
Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Connection: close are appended to the copied headers and the status head is sent. The upstream bytes are then collected into a buffer, and each time a 0x0A byte is appended the whole buffer, up to and including that newline, is sent as one chunk - its size in lowercase hexadecimal with no leading zeros, "
", the bytes, "
" - each chunk its own awaited write. When the stream ends normally, any bytes left after the last newline go out as one final chunk the same way. A stream error ends the loop silently and DROPS the unsent remainder. The terminating chunk "0

" is always sent, then the connection is cancelled and forgotten. For example the upstream bytes "data: hi

" go out as "9
data: hi

", then "1


", then "0

".
side_effects: one socket write per upstream line, plus one for a trailing remainder and one for the terminating chunk
failure_cases: an upstream stream error truncates the relay without an error frame and drops the bytes after the last newline; the terminating chunk is still sent
records.cancellation: cancelling the connection ends the relay
records.windows_path: Reproduce the per-line framing: flush a chunk at every 0x0A, write the size in lowercase hexadecimal, flush a trailing remainder only when the stream ends cleanly, and drop it on a stream error.
records.verification_method: contract fixture asserting the exact chunk bytes for a two-line payload, a payload that ends without a newline, and a stream that fails mid-line
records.b3_note: 1.7.0 relays event streams one chunk per line (hexadecimal size) plus a final remainder that a stream error drops, where B2 sent one "1\r\n"-framed chunk per byte (upstream_defects.md entry 10, which no longer holds).

records.title: A non-streaming response is buffered whole, one byte at a time, then sent with a Content-Length
records.preconditions: The upstream Content-Type does not contain text/event-stream.
records.expected_result: Every byte of the upstream stream is appended to an in-memory buffer, so nothing is sent until the upstream response is complete and a large tool result costs an O(n) per-byte loop. Content-Length with the buffer's byte count and Connection: close are appended, the status head and the buffer are sent as one write, and the connection is cancelled and forgotten. Unlike the SSE branch, a stream error here is NOT caught and propagates to the caller, which answers 502 {"error":"upstream request failed"} - on a connection whose response may already be partly written.
side_effects: holds the whole response in memory
failure_cases: a mid-stream upstream error escapes and triggers the caller's 502 path
records.windows_path: Reproduce the buffering and the asymmetric error handling between the two branches.
records.verification_method: contract fixture with a large body and one with a mid-stream failure

records.title: A proxy-generated response is a JSON error with three headers and closes the connection
records.preconditions: The proxy is refusing or failing a request.
records.expected_result: The head is "HTTP/1.1 <status> <reason phrase>\r\n" followed by, in this order, "Content-Type: application/json", "Content-Length: <byte count>", "Connection: close", each ended with CRLF, then a blank CRLF. The body follows. When the write completes the connection is cancelled and forgotten. jsonError escapes backslash to double backslash and double quote to backslash-quote, replaces each newline and each carriage return with a single space, and wraps the result as {"error":"<escaped>"} with no spaces around the colon.
failure_cases: this is the failure rendering
records.windows_path: Byte-identical head and body construction; providers parse these bodies.
records.verification_method: unit on the escaping plus a contract fixture on the bytes

records.title: The proxy maps twelve status codes to reason phrases and defaults to OK or Error
records.preconditions: A status head is being built.
records.expected_result: 200 "OK", 201 "Created", 202 "Accepted", 204 "No Content", 400 "Bad Request", 401 "Unauthorized", 404 "Not Found", 405 "Method Not Allowed", 411 "Length Required", 413 "Content Too Large", 500 "Internal Server Error", 502 "Bad Gateway". Any other status in 200..<300 is "OK" and anything else is "Error". The 405 row is never reached by this file - the proxy answers 400, 401, 411, 413, 502 and upstream statuses - and the 404 row is reached only when an upstream answers 404.
failure_cases: none
records.windows_path: Reproduce all twelve rows and both defaults, unused rows included.
records.verification_method: unit over the table and both defaults

records.title: The proxy tracks open connections and is never shut down during the app's life
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPProxy.swift:175-183 accept and forget - :176 state.withLock { $0.connections[ObjectIdentifier(connection)] = connection } | :177 connection.start(queue: queue) | :182 state.withLock { _ = $0.connections.removeValue(forKey: ObjectIdentifier(connection)) }

DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPProxy.swift:139-152 stop, which has zero call sites - :140 let (listener, open) = state.withLock { state -> (NWListener?, [NWConnection]) in | :145 state.running = false | :148 listener?.cancel() | :150 connection.cancel()
records.action: A connection is accepted or finished.
records.expected_result: Every accepted connection is stored by identity in a lock-guarded map, started on the proxy's own queue, and removed from the map when it is cancelled or its stream ends. stop() would cancel the listener and every open connection and clear running, but it has no call sites anywhere in the source: the proxy is started once from the store's initializer and runs until the process exits.
side_effects: the connection map grows and shrinks with traffic
failure_cases: a connection cancelled without going through forget would leak an entry; every cancel path in the file calls forget
records.cancellation: individual connections are cancelled; the listener never is
records.windows_path: The teardown entry point may be a no-op or omitted entirely, but never shut the proxy down where the source does not - an OAuth server would become unreachable mid-session.

records.title: signIn discovers the authorization server, mints PKCE and state, runs the callback server, then exchanges the code
records.preconditions: An OAuth server that is not signed in.
records.expected_result: In order: discover(url:) against the remote address; verifier = a 32-byte random token, base64url; challenge = the SHA-256 of the verifier, base64url; state = a 24-byte random token, base64url. Then runCallbackServer with the server's display name and the expected state; inside its ready callback, once the loopback port is known, clientRegistration runs and the authorization URL is built - a nil URL throws MCPOAuthError.metadataFailed("The authorization address isn't valid."). Finally exchangeCode runs with the returned code, the redirect URI and the verifier. Every step throws an MCPOAuthError whose errorDescription becomes the card's failure message.
side_effects: one or more metadata HTTP GETs
possibly one dynamic client registration POST
opens a loopback TCP listener and the user's default browser
records.persistence: on success the session is written to protected storage under "MCP <id> oauth"; a new registration is written under "MCP <id> oauth-client"
failure_cases: any of the eleven MCPOAuthError cases, rendered per PR-MCP-160
records.cancellation: cancelling the probe cancels the callback listener through the task-cancellation handler, and the pending continuation resumes with MCPOAuthError.cancelled
records.windows_path: Same order. The browser is opened with the OS default-handler call; do not embed a web view, which would change the user's session and cookie context. Protected storage is Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3), under the same account strings.
records.verification_method: integration test with a stub authorization server driving the whole flow

records.title: Discovery reads protected-resource metadata from the 401 challenge, or probes two well-known paths
records.expected_result: An unparseable address throws discoveryFailed("That address doesn't look like a URL."). A GET of the address with Accept: application/json and a 30-second timeout is made; only a 401 response is inspected, and every WWW-Authenticate header on it (matched case-insensitively, whether a single string or a list) is scanned for a resource_metadata parameter and a scope parameter, stopping once both are found. When a resource_metadata URL was found, it is fetched and authorization_servers[0], resource and scopes_supported are read from it. When it was NOT found, two candidates are tried in order: "<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource<path of the address>" then "<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"; the first that parses AND has either an authorization_servers array or a resource string is used and the loop stops. scopes_supported becomes the scope list only when it yields at least one non-empty name. When no scopes were found that way, the scopes from the challenge are used. issuer defaults to the address's origin; it is trimmed of leading and trailing "/" characters and, if empty, throws discoveryFailed("That address doesn't look like a URL."). Only authorization_servers[0] is ever used; later entries are ignored.
side_effects: one GET of the MCP address plus up to three metadata GETs
failure_cases: a non-401 answer or a network failure simply yields no challenge and falls through to the two candidates
no usable metadata anywhere -> metadataFailed with the last error detail
records.cancellation: each request is a cancellation point
records.windows_path: Same order, same two candidates, same single-issuer rule, and accept a bare unquoted resource_metadata value.
records.verification_method: contract fixture replaying a challenge-carrying 401 and one with no challenge

records.title: A WWW-Authenticate parameter is read quoted or bare up to the next comma or space
records.expected_result: Find the first occurrence of "<name>=" anywhere in the header (no token-boundary check, so a parameter name that is a suffix of another would mis-match). Trim the remainder of leading whitespace. When it starts with a double quote, the value is everything up to the next double quote, and an unterminated quote yields nil. Otherwise the value is the leading run of characters that are neither a comma nor a space. An empty value yields nil. challengeScopes splits the scope parameter on single spaces, drops empty names, and yields nil when nothing remains.
failure_cases: a malformed challenge yields nil and discovery falls back to the well-known candidates
records.windows_path: Same permissive parse; Stripe sends resource_metadata unquoted and would be lost by a strict RFC 9110 parser.
records.verification_method: unit with a quoted value, a bare value followed by a comma, and an unterminated quote

records.title: Authorization-server metadata is sought at up to four candidate URLs, path-first for an issuer with a path
records.expected_result: base = the issuer trimmed of leading and trailing "/". When the issuer parses and has a path that is neither empty nor "/", two candidates come first: "<origin>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server<path>" then "<origin>/.well-known/openid-configuration<path>". Then always: "<base>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server" and "<base>/.well-known/openid-configuration". Each is fetched in order; the first that parses and has a non-empty authorization_endpoint AND a non-empty token_endpoint wins and yields AuthServerMetadata(issuer: base, authorizationEndpoint, tokenEndpoint, registrationEndpoint: the registration_endpoint string or nil, resource, resourceScopes). A document missing either endpoint records the detail "It's missing the addresses needed to sign in." and the loop continues. Exhausting the candidates throws metadataFailed(lastError), where lastError is the detail from the LAST failure only.
failure_cases: metadataFailed rendered as "The server's sign-in details didn't make sense. <detail>", or without the detail when it is empty
records.cancellation: each GET is a cancellation point
records.windows_path: Same candidate order. Stripe's issuer https://access.stripe.com/mcp needs the path-after-well-known forms first; the rest answer at the path-first forms below them.
records.verification_method: contract fixture over a path-bearing and a path-free issuer

Only then reuse it, carrying client_secret when present. Any mismatch or missing piece falls through to a fresh dynamic registration.

records.windows_path: Same exact-string issuer comparison; a looser match would reuse a client registered with a different authorization server. Protected storage is Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3), under the same account strings.
records.verification_method: unit with a matching and a mismatching stored issuer

records.title: The callback server listens on an OS-assigned loopback port and redirects to /callback there
records.expected_result: TCP parameters with requiredLocalEndpoint 127.0.0.1 at any port, and NO interface-type constraint (unlike the proxy's listener, which pins loopback). A construction failure throws network("Couldn't listen for the sign-in reply."), which renders as just that sentence. On ready, the assigned port gives redirectURI = "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback"; the ready callback then registers the client, stores the redirect URI and client for the later handler, and opens the authorization URL in the default browser on the main thread. A failure inside that callback finishes the wait with the thrown error. A failed listener state gives network("The connection to the browser broke."); a cancelled state gives MCPOAuthError.cancelled -> "Sign-in was cancelled.". The completion is idempotent under a lock, so the first outcome wins and the listener is cancelled with it.
side_effects: opens a loopback TCP listener on an ephemeral port
failure_cases: the three network and cancellation messages above
records.cancellation: the task-cancellation handler cancels the listener, which resumes the continuation with .cancelled
records.windows_path: Bind 127.0.0.1 with an OS-assigned port and no interface-type constraint. Windows Firewall must not prompt for a loopback-only listener; verify that on a clean machine. Protected storage is Windows Credential Manager (OD-0008 B3), under the same account strings.
records.verification_method: integration test driving a real loopback callback

records.title: A sign-in that is not completed in the browser times out after 300 seconds
records.expected_result: A timer scheduled on the callback queue fires unconditionally at +300 seconds and finishes the wait with MCPOAuthError.timedOut -> "Sign-in timed out. Try again and complete it in the browser.". Because the completion is idempotent, a flow that already finished is unaffected and the timer is a no-op. The timer is not cancelled early, so it always fires once.
side_effects: cancels the listener when it is the first outcome
failure_cases: the timedOut message above becomes the card's failure text
records.cancellation: an earlier cancellation wins because finish is first-outcome-wins
records.windows_path: Same 300-second deadline and the same always-fires timer.
records.verification_method: integration test with a shortened, injected deadline

records.title: The callback server reads only the request head, giving up past 1 MiB with no reply
records.preconditions: A browser connected to the callback listener.
records.expected_result: Reading stops immediately, cancelling the connection, when the wait has already finished. Otherwise bytes accumulate until CR LF CR LF; the head is everything up to and including that terminator. When the stream completes, errors, or the buffer passes 1048576 bytes without a terminator, the connection is cancelled with no reply at all and no outcome is recorded.
failure_cases: a truncated request leaves the flow waiting until the 300-second timeout
records.cancellation: a finished wait short-circuits every further read
records.windows_path: Same 1 MiB cap and the same silent close.
records.verification_method: contract fixture sending an oversized head

records.title: The callback accepts only GET and only the /callback path
records.expected_result: Only the first line of the head is parsed, split on spaces. When it has fewer than two parts or the method is not exactly "GET", answer 405 with status text "Method Not Allowed" and body "<html><body>Method not allowed.</body></html>", then cancel the connection with no outcome recorded. When the target is neither exactly "/callback" nor prefixed "/callback?", answer 404 with status text "Not Found" and body "<html><body>Not found.</body></html>", then cancel with no outcome. Query items are parsed by prefixing "http://127.0.0.1" to the target.
side_effects: writes a small HTML body and closes the connection
failure_cases: neither rejection records an outcome, so the flow keeps waiting until the timeout
records.windows_path: Verbatim bodies and status texts, and the same no-outcome behavior: a favicon request must not abort a sign-in.
records.verification_method: contract fixture sending POST /callback and GET /favicon.ico

records.title: The callback checks provider error, then code, then state, and every outcome page is served with HTTP 200
records.preconditions: A GET of /callback with query items.
records.expected_result: In this exact order. 1) A non-empty "error" query item: the message is "error_description" when it is present and non-empty, else "The sign-in was refused (<error>)."; render the FAILURE page with status 200 and, after it is sent, finish with callbackFailed(message). 2) A missing or empty "code": failure page with "The browser didn't send back a code.", status 200, then callbackFailed with that same sentence. 3) A "state" that does not equal the expected state: failure page with "Sign-in didn't finish. Try again.", status 200, then MCPOAuthError.stateMismatch. 4) Otherwise the SUCCESS page, status 200; only AFTER the page is written is the stored redirect URI and client read, and a missing client or empty redirect URI finishes with callbackFailed("Sign-in didn't finish."), else the flow succeeds with the code, the redirect URI and the client. The page is always sent before the outcome is recorded, so the user sees a result even when the app then fails.
side_effects: writes an HTML page and closes the connection
records.persistence: success leads to a token exchange which writes the session
failure_cases: the four messages above; the state check is the CSRF defence and its message is deliberately vague
records.cancellation: not cancellable once a page is being written
records.windows_path: Same order, same status 200 for every outcome, same send-page-then-resume ordering.
records.verification_method: contract fixture over all four branches asserting the status and body each time

The head is exactly "HTTP/1.1 <status> <statusText>
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: <UTF-8 byte count>
Connection: close

", followed by the UTF-8 body. The completion closure runs from the send completion, which is what orders the page before the outcome.
failure_cases: none

records.verification_method: contract fixture on the bytes

records.title: The three OAuth HTTP helpers each use a 30-second timeout and collapse unexpected failures to a bare network error
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPOAuth.swift:790-793 formEncode - :791 let unreserved = CharacterSet(charactersIn: "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-._~") | :792 return value.addingPercentEncoding(withAllowedCharacters: unreserved) ?? value
records.action: Any OAuth HTTP call is made.
records.expected_result: All three use timeoutInterval 30. fetchJSON is a GET with Accept: application/json; a non-HTTP response throws network("The server didn't answer properly."); any other thrown error becomes network("") which renders as "The network didn't answer."; a non-2xx status or an unparseable body throws metadataFailed("The server answered <status>."). post sends JSON with Content-Type and Accept application/json and returns the data and response without checking the status. postForm builds the body as name=value pairs in the fields' order joined by "&", where every name and every value is percent-encoded as UTF-8 with only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, "-", ".", "_" and "~" left as they are (so ":", "/", "+", "=", "&" and a space are all escaped), falling back to the raw text when encoding returns nil; it sends that body with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded and Accept application/json, and likewise returns without checking the status. An unparseable URL in any of them throws network("That address isn't valid."). oauthErrorMessage returns the body's non-empty error_description, else its error, else nil. origin builds "<scheme>://<host>" plus ":<port>" when a port is present, and throws discoveryFailed("That address doesn't look like a URL.") when the scheme or host is missing or empty.

records.expected_result: Re-read <data root>/mcp/claude.json; a missing, unparseable or empty mcpServers object yields an empty array. Ids are iterated in sorted order. An entry counts as remote when its "type" is "http" OR it has a "url" string. Remote with allowsHTTP true: {"type": "http", "name": <id>, "url": <url>, "headers": [{"name": <k>, "value": <v>}, ...]} with header keys sorted. Remote with allowsHTTP false: rewritten as a stdio launch {"name": <id>, "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", <url>, then per sorted header key "--header" and the single string "<key>: <value>" with a colon and one space], "env": []} - env is an empty ARRAY, not an object, and there is no type key. Local: {"name": <id>, "command": <command or empty string>, "args": <the raw JSON array from the file>, "env": [{"name": <k>, "value": <v>}, ...]} with env keys sorted. This is the only producer of "mcp-remote" in the source, and its output never becomes a resolved server.
records.persistence: none; the array is passed as a session parameter
failure_cases: a missing file yields an empty array and the session gets no MCP servers
records.windows_path: Same shapes, including the empty env array and the "<key>: <value>" header string. It must run AFTER writeAll, because it reads the file.
records.verification_method: contract fixture over both capability values

records.title: Codex user servers named in ~/.codex/config.toml are switched off for the session by plain name only
records.expected_result: Return nil unless codex.json parses and its mcp_servers object is non-empty. Otherwise take that object and, for every name from codexUserServerNames that is not already a key, add {"enabled": false}. codexUserServerNames parses ~/.codex/config.toml line by line: trim; require the prefix "[mcp_servers."; drop it; require a "]" to exist and the text after it to be empty or start with "#"; take the text before the "]"; when it starts with a single or double quote the name is the content up to the matching same quote, else when it contains a dot the name is the part before the first dot, else the whole segment; trim it; DROP it entirely when it is empty or contains any whitespace, "[", "]", single quote, double quote, comma or dot; collect into a set and return it sorted. The file itself is never modified: enabled=false is a config override for the session only. A nested table path such as imap-email.env would name an entry that exists nowhere in the user's config and make Codex reject its whole configuration, failing every turn at once, which is why only bare names survive.
records.persistence: none; the user's own config file is never written
failure_cases: an unreadable config.toml yields an empty list and no overrides are added
records.windows_path: Same line parser and the same six-character rejection set. The home directory is the Windows user profile; the path is %USERPROFILE%\.codex\config.toml.
records.verification_method: unit over quoted, dotted, commented and malformed table headers

records.title: Three accessors return a path or content only when the file holds a non-empty server object
records.action: The launcher asks for MCP configuration.
records.expected_result: serversPresent is true only when the file reads, parses, and the named key holds a non-empty object. claudeConfigPath returns the path of claude.json or nil. geminiSettingsPath returns the path of gemini-settings.json or nil. copilotConfigJSON returns the WHOLE copilot.json re-serialized as a compact JSON string - not a path - or nil. A nil result makes the caller omit its MCP flag or environment variable entirely rather than pass an empty value (ClaudeSession.swift:96, MCPSessionOverrides.swift:15, ProviderRegistry.swift:285). There is no fourth accessor: nothing lists the connected server ids.
failure_cases: a missing file yields nil, which is the no-servers case
records.windows_path: Same nil-on-empty contract. copilotConfigJSON hands the whole compact JSON as a single argument value, not a file path, so it must survive command-line construction unmangled.
records.verification_method: unit over present, empty and missing files
records.b2_change: connectedIDs lost its only caller: B1 DroppyCode/Services/Providers/AntigravitySession.swift:83-84 passed its ids after "--allowed-mcp-server-names", deleted at B2 (see PR-MCP-175). The five accessors are unchanged (no diff in MCPProviderConfig.swift).
records.b3_note: 1.7.0 deletes connectedIDs (B2 MCPProviderConfig.swift:230-237), which had no caller; the other three accessors and serversPresent are unchanged.

records.title: Copilot arguments pass the config inline, disable the user's own servers by name, and disable built-ins only for github
records.expected_result: Return an empty array immediately when copilotConfigJSON is nil. Otherwise ids = the keys of mcpServers inside that JSON string, and the arguments are built in this exact order: "--additional-mcp-config" then the whole compact JSON as one argument; then, for each name from copilotUserServerNames (the sorted keys of mcpServers in ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json) that is NOT in ids, the pair "--disable-mcp-server" and that name; then "--disable-builtin-mcps" appended only when ids contains the exact id "github".
failure_cases: an unreadable user config yields no disable flags
records.windows_path: Same order and the same conditional flag. The JSON argument must be passed as one argv element; a shell-quoted command line would mangle it.
records.verification_method: unit over the three argument groups plus a launch test asserting the argument vector

records.title: OpenCode receives its whole configuration through an environment variable rebuilt from claude.json
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:281-283 - :283 if provider == .opencode || provider == .opencodeGo { environment.merge(MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment()) { _, new in new } }
records.preconditions: An OpenCode or OpenCode Go session is starting.
records.expected_result: Return an empty map when claude.json is missing, unparseable, or its mcpServers object is empty. For each member: when "type" is "http", emit {"type": "remote", "url": <url or the empty string>, "enabled": true} plus "headers" only when non-empty; otherwise require a non-empty "command" string or SKIP the member entirely, and emit {"type": "local", "command": [<command>] + <args>, "enabled": true} - command is an ARRAY whose first element is the executable - plus "environment" (not "env") only when non-empty. Return an empty map again when nothing was built. The root object is {"$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "mcp": <the map>}, serialized with sorted keys, returned as ["OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT": <that JSON string>]. Only string values survive the header and environment conversions; non-string values are dropped. The map is merged into the session environment for both the OpenCode and the OpenCode Go provider, the new value winning over an inherited one (ProviderRegistry.swift:283).
records.persistence: none; the value rides in the child environment
failure_cases: a local entry with an empty command is dropped silently
records.windows_path: Same key names, the command-as-array shape and the "environment" spelling. The whole JSON must survive environment-block construction; Windows environment variables have a large but finite size, so a very long configuration is a real limit to note. It applies to OpenCode Go as well as OpenCode.
records.verification_method: contract fixture comparing the emitted JSON string
records.b2_change: B1 DroppyCode/Services/Providers/ProviderRegistry.swift:272 `if provider == .opencode { environment.merge(MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment()) { _, new in new } }` -> B2 :275 `if provider == .opencode || provider == .opencodeGo { environment.merge(MCPSessionOverrides.opencodeEnvironment()) { _, new in new } }`: the new OpenCode Go provider (DroppyCode/Core/Models/Provider.swift:8 `case opencodeGo`, display name "OpenCode Go" at :27) receives the same environment. opencodeEnvironment itself is unchanged.
